# marram/php

> Marram API client for PHP 8.1+. Connects end users' third-party accounts, calls those
> providers' APIs through Marram, manages provider webhooks, and signs users in with OAuth2.
> Works with any PSR-18 HTTP client (auto-discovered). Holds the secret API key: server-side only.

This file is for AI coding assistants. Follow the rules first; the reference follows.

## Rules

1. **Never expose the API key.** Never echo it, put it in JavaScript, or send it to the browser.
   Browser code uses `@aszura/marram-browser`, which talks directly to Marram with a token
   you mint server-side.
2. **Connections belong to your user ID.** `connections->init` requires `externalUserId` — your
   own opaque ID for the user — and every later proxy, refresh, revoke and webhook call addresses
   the connection with that same ID. There is no Marram key to persist. Reconnecting the same
   user replaces their connection.
3. **PKCE on every connect and sign-in.** `init` takes a `codeChallenge`; `claim` needs the
   matching `codeVerifier`, the `claimCode` query parameter the redirect arrived with — and for
   connections the `flowId` init returned. Nothing is live until claimed. Keep the flowId and
   verifier together in the starting user's `$_SESSION`, or in the browser's `sessionStorage` via
   `@aszura/marram-browser`. A connect redirect carries `?status=connected&claimCode=…` — never
   a key. The `claimCode` is one-time and exists only in that redirect, so a flow can only be
   claimed from it.
4. **Claim once.** Single-use, expires 30 minutes after the provider step. `unset()` the stored
   verifier when you read it.
5. **Set `auth`, `redirectUrl` and the provider on the server.** If the request picks a provider,
   check it against an allowlist with `in_array(..., true)`.
6. **Branch on `$e->errorCode`, never `$e->getMessage()`.** Unknown codes: fall back to `$e->status`.
7. **Proxy responses are the provider's.** `$marram->proxy->request()` returns a PSR-7
   `ResponseInterface` for every provider status. Check `getStatusCode()` yourself. Only Marram's own
   refusals throw. It is **not signed**: don't run `Signature::verifyMessage` on it.
8. **Verify webhooks with the raw body** (`file_get_contents('php://input')`), never a
   re-encoded `json_decode` result.
9. All responses are associative arrays (shapes below), not objects. Exceptions:
   `ConnectionRedirect`, `ConnectToken` (objects) and proxy responses (PSR-7).
10. **Finish endpoint for `@aszura/marram-browser`? Use `Marram\ConnectFlow` /
    `Marram\SignInFlow`.** Their `serveFinish` / `replyFinish` serve a sign-in, or a connect
    started with `claim: 'server'`. Don't keep the provider in `$_SESSION`: the browser sends it
    with the finish payload. The package no longer calls their start side, which remains for
    browser code you write yourself.
11. **The browser package starts every flow with a token.** `$marram->connectToken($userId)` /
    `$marram->signInToken()` (needs `signingSecret:` on the Client) mint a short-lived token
    locally — no API call — and the browser runs the flow directly against Marram with
    `connect(provider, { token })` / `signIn(provider, { token })`. One token starts exactly one
    flow, does one browser `disconnect`, or starts one browser `setUpWebhook` (manual webhook
    setup); it can still claim its flow after it expires. Pass
    `redirectUrl:` when minting (no dashboard setup needed); without it the page's URL
    must be on the environment's redirect allowlist, and a set allowlist binds the token's URL too.
    Don't sign a URL taken from the browser unchecked. Sign-in claims always stay on your server
    with the API key.

## Install and create a client

```php
// composer require marram/php   (plus a PSR-18 client, e.g. guzzlehttp/guzzle)
$marram = new Marram\Client(
    apiKey: getenv('MARRAM_API_KEY'),
    // environment: 'staging',          // default 'production'
    // baseUrl: 'https://…/v1',          // overrides environment; include /v1
    // httpClient: $psr18Client,         // requestFactory:, streamFactory: also accepted
    // signingSecret: getenv('MARRAM_SIGNING_SECRET'), // for connectToken()/signInToken()
);
```

## Connect a user's account

```php
// Start (behind your login):
$pkce = Marram\Pkce::create();
$result = $marram->connections->init('google', [
    'auth' => 'oAuth2',
    'redirectUrl' => 'https://yourapp.com/connected',
    'codeChallenge' => $pkce['codeChallenge'],
    'codeChallengeMethod' => $pkce['codeChallengeMethod'], // 'S256'
    'externalUserId' => (string) $user->id,                // required: your opaque user id
]);
$_SESSION['marram_connect'] = ['flowId' => $result['flowId'], 'codeVerifier' => $pkce['codeVerifier']];
header('Location: ' . $result['authorizationUrl']);
exit;

// Return at /connected (lands with ?status=connected&claimCode=…), same browser session:
$redirect = Marram\ConnectionRedirect::parse($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']);
$pendingFlow = $_SESSION['marram_connect'] ?? null;
unset($_SESSION['marram_connect']);
if ($redirect->ok && $pendingFlow !== null) {
    $connection = $marram->connections->claim('google', $pendingFlow['flowId'], $pendingFlow['codeVerifier'], $redirect->claimCode);
    markConnected($user->id, $connection['providerKey']); // address it by $user->id from now on
} elseif (!$redirect->ok) {
    // $redirect->error, $redirect->errorMessage: declined or provider failure
}
```

## Serve `@aszura/marram-browser` (browser-side PKCE)

The browser package starts flows with a token you mint, and a sign-in, or a connect started with
`claim: 'server'`, finishes at an endpoint you mount with `ConnectFlow` (or `SignInFlow`). It runs
behind your own login. `serveStart` / `replyStart` remain for browser code you write yourself.

```php
$connect = new Marram\ConnectFlow(
    $marram,
    ['google', 'trello'],                 // allowlist; or ['trello' => ['integrationKey' => '…', 'auth' => 'oAuth1']]
    'https://yourapp.com/connected',      // or fn (string $provider): string
    // auth: 'oAuth2', theme: 'light'|'dark'
);

// Plain PHP: reads php://input, sets the status, echoes JSON.
// POST /marram/start
$connect->serveStart(externalUserId: (string) $user->id);
// POST /marram/finish
$connect->serveFinish(function (array $claimed) use ($user): array {
    markConnected($user->id, $claimed['connection']['providerKey']);
    return ['connected' => true];         // answered as JSON; null answers ['ok' => true]
});

// Laravel / Symfony / any framework: the same as ['status' => int, 'body' => array].
$reply = $connect->replyStart($request->json()->all(), externalUserId: (string) $user->id);
return response()->json($reply['body'], $reply['status']);
$reply = $connect->replyFinish($request->json()->all(), fn (array $claimed) => save($claimed));

// Lowest level, throwing instead of replying:
$started = $connect->start($input, externalUserId: '…'); // ['provider', 'flowId', 'authorizationUrl']
$claimed = $connect->finish($input);                      // ['provider', 'flowId', 'connection' => [...]]
```

`ConnectFlow::start` requires `externalUserId` (the connection's identity) and refuses to start
without one. `SignInFlow($marram, $providers, $redirectUrl, ?theme)` is the same for sign-in:
start answers `['provider', 'sessionKey', 'authorizationUrl']`, finish gives
`['provider', 'sessionKey', 'user', 'raw']`.

Input: start takes `{provider, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256'}`, finish takes
`{provider, flowId|sessionKey, codeVerifier, claimCode}`, exactly what the browser package sends. Bad
input throws `Marram\FlowInputException` (`$status` 400, `$errorCode` `UNKNOWN_PROVIDER` or
`INVALID_INPUT`). `reply*` / `serve*` answer `['code', 'error', 'requestId'?]`: 400 for bad input
or a claim Marram refused (`CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `CODE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH`,
`MISSING_PKCE_PARAMETERS`, `CLAIM_CODE_MISMATCH`, `MISSING_CLAIM_CODE`), 502 for any other `MarramException`; anything else is rethrown.
`Marram\Flow::errorReply(\Throwable $e)` gives that reply (or null) for your own handlers, and
`$connect->providers()` lists the allowlist.

## Sign users in

```php
$pkce = Marram\Pkce::create();
$result = $marram->sessions->init('google', [
    'auth' => 'oAuth2',
    'redirectUrl' => 'https://yourapp.com/signed-in',
    'codeChallenge' => $pkce['codeChallenge'],
    'codeChallengeMethod' => 'S256',
]);
$_SESSION['marram'] = ['sessionKey' => $result['sessionKey'], 'codeVerifier' => $pkce['codeVerifier']];
// redirect to $result['authorizationUrl'], then at /signed-in?sessionKey=…&claimCode=…:
$pending = $_SESSION['marram'];
unset($_SESSION['marram']);
$info = $marram->sessions->claim('google', $pending['sessionKey'], $pending['codeVerifier'], (string) ($_GET['claimCode'] ?? ''));
$info['user']; // normalized user; $info['raw'] is the provider's payload
```

## Call a provider's API

```php
$response = $marram->proxy->request('GET', 'trello', '1/members/me/boards', $userId);
if ($response->getStatusCode() >= 400) { /* provider error */ }
$boards = json_decode((string) $response->getBody(), true);

$marram->proxy->request(
    'POST', 'github', 'repos/acme/app/issues', $userId,
    body: ['title' => 'Bug'],                         // sent as JSON
    query: ['per_page' => '50'],
    headers: ['Accept' => 'application/vnd.github+json'],
    // contentType: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded', version: '2022-11-28', integrationKey: '…',
);
```

`$path` must be non-empty and contain no `..` segment. Caller headers starting with `x-marram-`
are dropped.

Async: `$marram->proxy->enqueue($method, $provider, $path, $userId, $callbackUrl, ...)`
returns `['requestId' => …]` (HTTP 202). The provider's response is POSTed to `$callbackUrl`
(public HTTPS). Verify it with `Signature::verifyWebhook`.

## Webhooks

```php
$raw = file_get_contents('php://input');
if (!Marram\Signature::verifyWebhook(getallheaders(), $raw, getenv('MARRAM_SIGNING_SECRET'))) {
    http_response_code(401);
    exit;
}
$event = json_decode($raw, true);
```

`$secrets` may be an array during rotation. Default tolerance is 300 s. It never throws.
`Signature::verifyMessage($psr7Message, $secrets)` works on PSR-7 requests/responses and rewinds the
body. `Signature::verify($body, $timestamp, $signature, $secrets)` is the low-level form.

```php
$marram->webhooks->register('github', $userId, body: [/* kind-specific */], kind: 'push', metadata: 'repo-42');
$marram->webhooks->list('github', $userId);
$marram->webhooks->get('github', $webhookKey, $userId);
$marram->webhooks->update('github', $webhookKey, $userId, body: [...]);
$marram->webhooks->delete('github', $webhookKey, $userId);
$manual = $marram->webhooks->initManual('stripe', $userId, redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/done');
// paste $manual['ingressUrl'] at the provider, send the user to $manual['setupUrl']
```

`delete` answers `unregisteredAtProvider`: `false` for a manual webhook or one whose connection was
revoked, which Marram clears without calling the provider. The provider may still hold it; remove
it in the provider's dashboard. Revoking or disconnecting a user leaves their webhooks running until
you delete them. The browser SDK's `setUpWebhook` starts a manual setup with a connect token (Marram
picks the `webhookKey`); `initManual` is the API-key form, needed for a custom key or metadata.

## API reference

All methods throw `Marram\MarramException` on a Marram error. `?string $integrationKey` is
only needed when a provider has several integrations and no default.

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `connections->init(string $provider, array{auth, redirectUrl, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256', externalUserId, theme?: 'light'|'dark'} $body, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{flowId, authorizationUrl, message?}` |
| `connections->claim(string $provider, string $flowId, string $codeVerifier, string $claimCode)` | Connection array |
| `connections->refresh(string $provider, string $externalUserId, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | Connection array (409 `CONFLICT` if a refresh is running) |
| `connections->revoke(string $provider, string $externalUserId, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `void`. The browser SDK's `disconnect` does this with a connect token, for the token's own user. The user's webhooks keep running until deleted |
| `connections->get(string $provider, string $externalUserId, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | Connection array (no refresh, no provider call; 404 `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, 410 `CONNECTION_REVOKED`) |
| `connections->list(string $provider, string $integrationKey)` | `list<Connection>` |
| `sessions->init(string $provider, array{auth: 'oAuth2', redirectUrl, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod, externalUserId?, theme?} $body, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{sessionKey, authorizationUrl, message?}` |
| `sessions->claim(string $provider, string $sessionKey, string $codeVerifier, string $claimCode)` | `array{user, raw}` |
| `sessions->userinfo(string $provider, string $sessionKey, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{user, raw}` |
| `sessions->refresh(string $provider, string $sessionKey)` | Session array |
| `sessions->revoke(string $provider, string $sessionKey, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `void` |
| `sessions->get(string $provider, string $sessionKey)` | Session array (no refresh, no provider call; 404 `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, 410 `SESSION_REVOKED`) |
| `sessions->list(string $provider, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `list<Session>` |
| `proxy->request(string $method, string $provider, string $path, string $externalUserId, mixed $body = null, array $query = [], array $headers = [], ?string $integrationKey = null, ?string $version = null, ?string $contentType = null)` | `Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface` |
| `proxy->enqueue(string $method, string $provider, string $path, string $externalUserId, string $callbackUrl, …same optional args)` | `array{requestId}` |
| `webhooks->register(string $provider, string $externalUserId, array $body = [], ?string $kind = null, ?string $webhookKey = null, ?string $metadata = null, ?string $version = null, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{success, webhookKey, providerWebhookId?, kind?}` |
| `webhooks->list(string $provider, string $externalUserId, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `list<Webhook>` |
| `webhooks->get(string $provider, string $webhookKey, string $externalUserId, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | Webhook array |
| `webhooks->update(string $provider, string $webhookKey, string $externalUserId, array $body = [], ?string $version = null, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{success, webhookKey, …}` |
| `webhooks->delete(string $provider, string $webhookKey, string $externalUserId, ?string $version = null, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{success, webhookKey, unregisteredAtProvider, …}` |
| `webhooks->initManual(string $provider, string $externalUserId, ?string $redirectUrl = null, ?string $integrationKey = null)` | `array{sessionId, webhookKey, setupUrl, ingressUrl, status: 'pending', fields}`. The browser SDK's `setUpWebhook` does this with a connect token |
| `environment->integrations()` | `list<array>` |
| `environment->identityProviders()` | `list<array>` — enabled for sign-in, filtered by release status. The browser SDK's `listIdentityProviders` fetches a trimmed list with a sign-in token |
| `environment->providers(?string $externalUserId = null)` | `list<array>` — what a user can connect; with `$externalUserId`, each integration's `connected`/`connectionStatus` is that user's, else null. The browser SDK's `listProviders` fetches the same list with a connect token |

Browser-flow classes: `Marram\ConnectFlow(Client $marram, array $providers, string|\Closure $redirectUrl, string $auth = 'oAuth2', ?string $theme = null)`
and `Marram\SignInFlow(Client $marram, array $providers, string|\Closure $redirectUrl, ?string $theme = null)`,
both with `start(mixed $input, ?string $externalUserId = null)`, `finish(mixed $input)`,
`replyStart(mixed $input, ?string $externalUserId = null)`, `replyFinish(mixed $input, callable $onClaimed)`
→ `['status' => int, 'body' => array]`, `serveStart(?string $externalUserId = null)`,
`serveFinish(callable $onClaimed)`, `providers()`; `Marram\FlowInputException` (`$status`, `$errorCode`);
`Marram\Flow::errorReply(\Throwable $e)`.

Static helpers: `Marram\Pkce::create()` → `['codeVerifier', 'codeChallenge', 'codeChallengeMethod' => 'S256']`;
`Marram\ConnectionRedirect::parse(string $url)` → object with `ok`, `claimCode`, `error`, `errorMessage`
(`error` is `'missing_status'` when the URL carries neither `status=connected` nor `error`,
`'missing_claim_code'` when a connected redirect has no `claimCode`);
`Marram\Signature::verifyWebhook / verifyMessage / verify`.

Tokens (`$expiresIn` over 600 throws): `$marram->connectToken(string $externalUserId, ?string $provider = null, ?string $integrationKey = null, int $expiresIn = 600, ?string $redirectUrl = null)`
and `$marram->signInToken(?string $externalUserId = null, …)` → `Marram\ConnectToken` object
with `token`, `jti` (echoed by the claim, so you can match results to the token you issued) and
`expiresAt`. Both need `signingSecret:` on the Client. `Marram\ConnectToken::mint(...)` is the
standalone signer.

Connection array keys: `externalUserId, providerKey, integrationKey, providerUserId?, authType,
status, grantedScopes?, expiresAt?, lastRefreshedAt?, lastUsedAt?, lastError?, lastErrorAt?,
createdAt, updatedAt, disconnectedAt?`. Session arrays have the same keys plus `sessionKey`.
`authType` is one of `oAuth1, oAuth2, api_key, basic, session`. `status` is one of `active,
pending, reauth_required, error, revoked, inactive`.

## Errors

```php
try {
    $marram->connections->refresh('google', $userId);
} catch (Marram\MarramException $e) {
    $e->status;     // HTTP status
    $e->errorCode;  // stable code; "HTTP_<status>" if none was sent
    $e->requestId;  // quote in support requests
    $e->body;       // decoded JSON or raw text
    if ($e->errorCode === 'CONFLICT') { /* refresh already running; retry shortly */ }
}
```

Common codes: `INVALID_API_KEY`, `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RATE_LIMITED`,
`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `CONFLICT`, `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND`, `INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND`,
`INTEGRATION_KEY_REQUIRED` (pass `$integrationKey`), `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`,
`WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND`, `MISSING_EXTERNAL_USER_ID`, `MISSING_FLOW_ID`, `MISSING_PKCE_PARAMETERS`,
`CODE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH` (wrong or reused verifier; start again), `AUTH_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`,
`BLOCKED_PATH`; token flows add `INVALID_CONNECT_TOKEN`, `CONNECT_TOKEN_EXPIRED`,
`CONNECT_TOKEN_REUSED`, `CONNECT_TOKEN_WRONG_USE`, `REDIRECT_URL_NOT_ALLOWED`. The full list is in
`openapi.yaml` under `components.schemas.Error`.
